howToApply: Base: main. These are two NEW batches (whole-year content), not edits to 2026-11/2026-12.
Do the code change in codeChanges FIRST, on its own feature branch; the sight-word items need it to play correctly.
Write each snapshots[] entry to its path (fields url, title, retrievedAt, scope, content).

Create content/paced/2026-27-k-sight-words/review.json from newItems with id starting 'K-sw-', and content/paced/2026-27-decoding/review.json from ids containing '-dc-'. Keep the 'topic' and 'spokenTarget' fields when building.
approvals.json for each batch: use the teacher's decisions from the review once given; until then nothing ships.

Run python3 scripts/build-paced-batch.py <batch> for both, the five validators, add tests (incl. spokenTarget never appears in question or choices-as-prompt), then the release flow (Preview, Trace checks, then main).

codeChanges.what: Four Corners: optional item field spokenTarget (string). When present, the screen must NOT show the word. Show the banner 'LISTEN: TEACHER SAYS THE WORD', a 'Say the word' button (speechSynthesis, same as Spelling Bee/Quick Check Read it to me), and a small teacher-only 'Show word' toggle that hides again on Next. Reveal shows the explanation as usual. Validator: spokenTarget is one of choices and never appears in question text.
codeChanges.why: Handoff notes 'spoken-target sight-word recognition remains a coverage gap'; showing the word in the prompt lets kids just match letters.

codeChanges.what: Quick Check draws Four Corners items too. Support spokenTarget the same way there (Read it to me speaks the target; word hidden until Reveal), or exclude spokenTarget items from Quick Check until it does.

NOT now. Trace's idea for later: a pregame 'Topic' setting (e.g. Four Corners with only Sight Words). Items already carry topic: 'sight-words', 'syllable-types', 'syllable-division' so the filter is easy to add.

snapshots.title: Decoding Strategies handout (LETRS, Moats & Tolman), shared at Sweetwater PL Nov 2026
snapshots.scope: Full text of the one-page handout.
snapshots.content:
Break it down. Sound it out. Read it!
1 Consonant between the vowels: Underline the vowels. When a word has 1 consonant in between the vowels, draw a line before the consonant. If the word doesn't make sense, draw a line after the consonant. Read each syllable. Read the whole word. robot: ro bot
2 Consonants between the vowels: When a word has 2 consonants in between the vowels, draw a line between the consonants. Keep vowel teams, blends, and digraphs together (ea, st, mp, ch, or ph). picnic: pic nic
More Than 2 Consonants between the Vowels: When a word has more than 2 consonants in between the vowels, draw a line between the consonants. Keep vowel teams, blends, and digraphs together. dolphin: dol phin
Smaller Steps = Stronger Readers!

snapshots.title: 6 Syllable Types handout (Thrive Literacy Corner), shared at Sweetwater PL Nov 2026
snapshots.scope: Full text of the one-page handout.
snapshots.content:
closed: ends in a consonant, short vowel sound (cat)
open: ends with a vowel, vowel has long sound (go)
magic e: ends with a silent e, long vowel sound, 1 consonant between the vowel and silent e (cake)
vowel team: 2 vowels making 1 sound (boat)
r controlled: at least 1 vowel followed by r; ar, er, ir, or, ur (star)
consonant -le: ends with a consonant and -le (turtle)
